decisions.advocate: Do not park on this: the reported behavior is the fail-closed reading of an ambiguous spec, the "obvious" fix opens a real evasion hole, and no legitimate workflow reaches the scenario — record it as a spec-ambiguity item with one added test at the next gate.
decisions.decision: continue; file a spec-ambiguity note and add a pinning test before the change closes, do not change dropped_eval_cases's behavior
decisions.head: 07f6d6818ec24178edc6567abd274ea00a8b15c3
decisions.item: adversarial reviewer says escalate: plugin/gate/checks.py: dropped_eval_cases's new `dot_dropped` set (introduced by this exact round's fix) is unioned into the result unconditionally -- `dropped = set(dot_dropped) | {...filtered by survivor_cases...}` -- never filtered against `survivor_cases`. So when one file of a multi-file eval case is renamed to a dot-prefixed destination while a sibling file in the same, original (visible) case folder is left untouched, the whole case is reported as a drop even though the sibling still exists and is visible at HEAD. Traced with real `tree_files` semantics (git ls-tree lists every blob, dot-prefixed or not, so the sibling's path, e.g. `evals/cases/foo/b.yaml`, is genuinely a survivor and `case_of()` maps it back to `foo`): the source case name still lands in `survivor_cases`, yet the unconditional `set(dot_dropped)` union reports it dropped anyway.; This directly contradicts the design invariant both spec.md ('A case is dropped when no path remains, at HEAD's committed tree, under its folder ... so that one file dropped out of a multi-file case while a sibling survives is never mistaken for the whole case's drop') and plan.md's Risks section state for this exact function -- the invariant is honored for a plain `D` (proven by `test_ratchets_eval_case_partial_delete_is_not_a_drop`) but not for a dot-prefixed rename of one file in a multi-file case, which has no test at all.; This is a false-positive in the gate's own deterministic ratchets check (the subject of this whole change), which runs at phases (c)/(d)/(e) for every change, in every project the plugin drives (intent.md's own 'Affected users and systems' -- wide blast radius). A legitimate partial reorganisation of a multi-file eval case that happens to dot-rename one file would incorrectly park the change on an undeclared 'ratchet: evals' hit for the whole case, not just the renamed file.; Confirmed this is newly introduced by the code under review, not a pre-existing accepted gap: before this round's fix there was no separate `dot_dropped` set at all (the owner's bug report was about the destination also being added to `touched`); the fix replaced that with a `dot_dropped` set that bypasses the same survivor-based filtering `touched` otherwise goes through, which is what creates the gap.; No existing or added test exercises this scenario (a dot-rename of one case file alongside an untouched, surviving sibling in the same source case folder), so the whole suite (including this round's own two targeted fixes) passes with this bug present -- angle 6 (the tests) finds nothing here that would catch it.
rationale: Spec's dot clause ('an R whose destination starts with "." is a drop') reads as unconditional; the survivor-emptiness sentence that follows explains the general rule's HEAD-tree rationale, not an exception to the dot clause — the intersection is genuinely unspecified, not a proven contradiction.
Both verdicts agree the current code is undertested for this exact case; they disagree only on which direction the gap should resolve.

The safer reading for a gate check built to stop an agent lowering the bar is fail-closed: a false-positive park costs one owner label (declare in plan or accept-risk), while the reviewer's proposed filter creates a real evasion — rename the targeted file to a dot folder, leave any sibling in place, and the whole-case hit vanishes.

Decision 11/21 already treats a failed deterministic check as a park the owner clears cheaply, so the current over-inclusive behavior is within the designed cost asymmetry, not a defect that must block this build.

Next: add a test pinning dot-rename-with-surviving-sibling as a drop, and one spec.md sentence stating the dot rule is evaluated independently of the survivor rule, so the semantics are settled for future rounds.
decisions.reviewer: Escalate: send back to fix `dropped_eval_cases`'s unconditional union of `dot_dropped`.
